name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg70 sits on the extracellular Ig-V domain at the CD80/CD86 contact surface, and Arg70Trp removes the charged contact and adds a bulky indole, so CTLA-4 binds its ligands weakly and transendocytoses less ligand.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E3", "E4", "E20", "E2", "E1"], "would_refute": "Superposing R70W onto the CTLA-4/B7-1 (1I8L) and CTLA-4/B7-2 (1I85) complexes shows residue 70 with no atom within about 4.5 \u00c5 of CD80, CD86 or ICOSLG, and the mutant side chain clashes with nothing and loses no contacts.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Only evidence that names this exact residue points here: UniProt records strongly reduced CD80/CD86/ICOSLG interaction for residue 70 (E3). The ALPS-linked pathogenic call (E1, E2) and the transendocytosis assay (E4) fit a ligand-contact loss. Ranked first because it is the only residue-specific functional result. Still missing: the contact map that places residue 70 in the interface (G6), and any direct binding or transendocytosis data for R70W (G1)."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg70 lies in the Ig-V beta-sheet region (strand 68-77), and the Arg-to-Trp change disturbs local packing or a buried salt bridge, lowering folding stability so that less correctly folded CTLA-4 reaches the cell surface.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E10", "E9", "E12", "E14", "E15", "E16"], "would_refute": "Residue 70 side chain is solvent-exposed in the 9DQ3, 1I8L and 1I85 structures with no buried salt bridge or hydrogen-bond network partner, and stability predictors (for example FoldX or Rosetta ddG) give R70W a change near zero (|ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol) while the structure-based contact analysis still shows the same ligand contacts as wild type.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Indirect support only. Residue 70 is conserved (E16) and inside a beta strand (E10), and the in-silico scores are mixed: AlphaMissense is ambiguous (E12) and EVE is uncertain (E15), while popEVE is more deleterious (E14). None of these measures folding directly, and no stability data exist for this variant (G1, G2). It ranks below H1 because it is not tied to a residue-specific functional result."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The mutant folds and binds ligand normally but is retained or mistrafficked inside the cell, so less CTLA-4 reaches the surface to engage CD80/CD86 and the ligand-uptake function is reduced.", "mechanism_class": "other", "supports": ["E6", "E8", "E4", "E21"], "would_refute": "Surface-expression or transendocytosis measurements show R70W at wild-type surface levels and wild-type ligand uptake, or a structure-based check finds residue 70 buried against the core so that the substitution is only a folding defect with no trafficking consequence.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "Weakest of the three. It rests on general trafficking sensitivity of the ligand-uptake assay (E6) and on haploinsufficiency with incomplete penetrance (E8, E21) rather than on anything about R70W. No retrieved source tests surface expression for this variant (G1, G4). It is kept as a rival because it can't be excluded yet, and it differs in class from H1 and H2."}

name: record_handoff
arguments: {"to": "orchestrator", "summary": "Three agent-generated hypotheses are recorded for CTLA4 p.Arg70Trp. H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1): R70W weakens CD80/CD86/ICOSLG binding, favoured by UniProt mutagenesis E3. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2): R70W destabilises the Ig-V strand, supported only indirectly by conservation and mixed predictors. H3 (other, rank 3): R70W causes trafficking retention, which is weakly supported. The next test should superpose R70W on the 1I8L and 1I85 complexes (refutes H1 if no contact is lost) and run a ddG estimate (refutes H2 if |ddG| is near zero).", "refs": ["E3", "E4", "E10", "E12", "E14", "E15", "E18", "E19", "G1", "G2", "G6"]}
